2610.05223.title: Look Before You Leap: Thermodynamic Arbitration of Parametric and Non-Parametric Knowledge in LLM Agents via Self-Regulating Memory Architectures
2610.05223.paper_summary: The architecture of modern LLMs consists of a profound cognitive polarization. LLMs possess implicit intuition encoded in their parameters, yet rely on a disconnected, explicit mechanism to access the outside world. Agentic frameworks have not bridged this gap; instead, models are often compelled into pathological "induced amnesia." Under the prevailing "Retrieve-Always" paradigm, agents must distrust their internal knowledge, making every user interaction a "tabula rasa" event that must be checked externally. This creates reflexive dependence that can be thermodynamically wasteful, cognitively fragile, and susceptible to irrelevant context. We propose a return to first principles, operationalizing the biological maxim "Look Before You Leap." We introduce MARTA (Metacognitive Adaptive Retrieval and Thought Architecture), a neuro-symbolic framework that bridges parametric and non-parametric knowledge. Rather than treating retrieval as mandatory, MARTA models it as a cost, taking the leap only when perceived internal inadequacy warrants external information. By allowing the agent to gauge the entropy of its own thoughts before acting, MARTA enables deliberative retrieval and uncertainty-aware decision making. Our approach suggests that giving agents the capacity for introspection can restore a more efficient balance between internal knowledge and external information.
2610.05223.paper_summary_zh: 現代大型語言模型（LLMs）的架構由深刻的認知極化組成。LLMs 擁有隱含的直覺，這些直覺編碼在它們的參數中，但卻依賴一個斷裂的、明確的機制來接觸外部世界。代理框架並未彌合這一鴻溝；相反，模型常常被迫進入病態的「誘發性健忘」。在當前的「總是檢索」範式下，代理必須不信任其內部知識，使得每次用戶互動都成為一個必須外部檢查的「白板」事件。這造成了反射性依賴，這種依賴在熱力學上可能是浪費的，在認知上是脆弱的，並且容易受到無關上下文的影響。我們提議回歸基本原則，將生物學格言「三思而後行」具體化。我們介紹了 MARTA（元認知自適應檢索與思維架構），這是一個橋接參數性和非參數性知識的神經符號框架。MARTA 將檢索視為一種成本，而不是強制性的，僅在感知到內部不足時才進行外部信息的獲取。通過允許代理在行動之前評估自身思維的熵，MARTA 使得深思熟慮的檢索和意識到不確定性的決策成為可能。我們的方法表明，賦予代理內省的能力可以恢復內部知識與外部信息之間更高效的平衡。
2610.05223.author: Akash Das et.al.
